requirement:
`habeas mdbook` MUST NOT require a separate authored coverage chapter or
`{coverage-index}` directive, or use such a directive to control generation
of the subchapter under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
The generated coverage subchapter MUST have no authored source file or edit
target.
rationale:
Obligations derived from `requirements.test-coverage.index.source`: (1) `habeas mdbook` must not require a separate authored coverage chapter. (2) It must not require a `{coverage-index}` directive. (3) It must not use such a directive to control generation of the subchapter. (4) The generated subchapter must have no authored source file or edit target.

Coverage:
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authored_coverage_directives_do_not_control_generated_placement]` is marked `{test}` for the subject. It builds a book with only a requirements-index chapter plus one unrelated authored chapter, and no authored coverage chapter or SUMMARY entry. It runs the production `populate_in` over three authored contents: plain text, one `:::{coverage-index}` directive, and two directives.
  - Obligations 1 to 3: in every case exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" chapter exists. It sits at `reports/coverage.md` and is the first child of the requirements index (`parent_names == ["Requirements index"]`). A directive in an authored chapter therefore neither adds a second report nor moves the generated one. The authored chapter's content is unchanged and it has no children.
  - Obligation 4: `source_path` is `None`, and no `md/reports/coverage.md` file is created.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` is also marked `{test}` for the subject. It runs with no authored coverage chapter (obligation 1). It asserts `source_path.is_none()` for the generated coverage chapter and for each generated page, under both numbered and unnumbered parents (obligation 4). It also asserts that no `:::{coverage-index}` directive is left in the generated content.

The edit target comes from the chapter's source path. The assertions on `source_path` and on the absence of a source file cover it.

I found no gap. Neither test puts a directive in the requirements-index chapter itself. The requirement does not single that case out, and the tested placement does not depend on any directive. I found no acknowledgments, and none were needed.
